In this lesson, you will learn about the operation of a sawtooth generator.
INTRODUCTIONM
The sawtooth generator changes a squarewave input to a sawtooth output..
Unlike an oscillator, the sawtooth generator requires an input signal and does not use feedback.
For this reason, the sawtooth generator can be thought of as a wave-shaper.

Sawtooth generators change square waves to sawtooth waves..
DISCUSSION
The square wave input is clamped or held at a DC level by C1, R1 and the base-to-collector junction of Q1.
The AC square wave input becomes a DC square wave.
When this DC square wave goes positive, Q1 is reverse biased and does not conduct.
When the DC square wave drops to zero, Q1 is forward biased and conducts.
When Q1 conducts, C2 discharges through it very quickly.
The frequency of the output is determined solely by the frequency of the input.
The linearity (how straight) of the output is also determined by the input frequency.
A low input frequency allows the capacitor to charge for a longer period of time. The output shows more of the charge curve. It is not linear.
CHARGE CURVE - Capacitors do not charge at a constant rate. The chart below illustrates the action.
DEFINITION
Because the capacitor charges longer, the output amplitude is greater.
A high input frequency only allows the capacitor to charge for a short period of time. The amplitude is reduced.
The output shows only the first part of the charge curve. The output is very linear or straight.
The DC supply voltage (Vcc) only effects the output amplitude. A high Vcc has a higher output amplitude than a low Vcc.
The output linearity and frequency are unaffected by the amount of Vcc.
A low frequency input produces a non-linear output when 20 VDC or 5VDC is applied.
A high frequency input produces a linear output when 20 VDC or 5 VDC is applied.
The amount of Vcc affects the output amplitude and has no effect on the linearity.
The RC time constant (TC) of R2 and C2 will effect the output.
A long TC produces a linear output having low amplitude. This effects the circuit in the same way as a high frequency input does.
A short TC produces a non-linear output having high amplitude. This effects the circuit in the same way as a low frequency input does.
What three factors reduce the output of a sawtooth generator?
Low Vcc reduces the output, but a low input frequency or a short RC time constant increases the output amplitude.

SAWTOOTH GENERATOR OP

In this experiment, you will measure input and output waveforms of a sawtooth generator. You will vary the input frequency and Vcc voltage and observe the effect on the output to verify normal operation..
EXPERIMENT
Pick up the PC130-43A card. The purpose of this card is to demonstrate the operation of sawtooth generators.
Compare the components on PC130-43A to the schematic shown.
The transistor functions as a switch. When OFF, Vcc charges C2 or C3 through R2. When ON, C2 or C3 is discharged from ground through Q1.
S1 selects between C2 and C3 to alter the RC time constant of the circuit.
1. Set the Test Console controls to the initial control settings..........
2. Carefully plug PC130-43A into the Test Console PC1 position.
3. Set S1 on PC130-43A to the C3 position.

MEASUREMENT SETUP - Carefully connect the oscilloscope to TP2.
